label: Add Bone
params_doc: {from? (instance or shape id: the bone starts on it) | parent? (bone id: the bone starts on its end; for a bone inside a shape, on its joint), to (instance or shape id: the bone moves it as a whole), head?: [x, y] (the joint on a root, stage px, default its registration point; from something that hangs from a bone the joint is always that bone's end, so chains stay joined), tail?: [x, y] (default `to`'s registration point), name?} → {bone, layer}. Both go to an armature layer (made for the first bone). Instances and shapes mix in one armature: a bone inside a shape can carry an instance (parent), and a bone can end on a shape that then gets bones of its own (bone.add_in_shape with parent)

label: Add Bone in Shape
params_doc: {shape? (shape id: the first bone, or another bone from the shape), parent? (bone id: continue the chain from its end; a bone that ends on a shape starts that shape's first bone inside it), head?: [x, y] (the joint, stage px; default the parent bone's end), tail: [x, y] (stage px), name?} → {bone, layer, created, points, shape}. The first bone moves the shape to an armature layer of its own, as an object (merge drawing leaves it alone), unless a bone already moves it; the shape's points are bound to the nearest bones inside it. An armature may hold several shapes with bones

label: Bind Points
params_doc: {bone, points?: [point index…] (default every point; see bone.info with points), mode?: "only" (the points follow just this bone; default) | "add" (they share it with the bones they follow) | "remove" | "auto" (back to automatic binding)} → {bone, changed, bound (how many points the bone moves)}. A shape armature's binding: which points of the shape follow which bone

label: Enable Springs
params_doc: {enabled: bool, layer? (the armature layer) | bone?} turns the armature's springs on or off (off: it plays its keyed poses exactly, as while posing)

label: Armatures
params_doc: {frame?, layer?, points?: bool} → every armature on the scene at the frame: its bones with joint and end (stage px, as keyed), joint angle and limits (°), slide and translation limits (px), spring (0–100) and its swing at the frame (°, what the spring adds to the angle), pinned; whether springs are on; the armature's members and whether it is mixed; each shape with bones (shapes: its bones, how many points, and with points every point on the stage with the bones it follows), the shape each bone is inside and how many points it moves; `shape` and `points` are the first shape's

label: Paint Weights
params_doc: {bone, at: [[x, y]…] (dab centres, stage px, at most 4096), radius? (px, 1–2000, default 20), strength? (0–100 at the centre, default 25), mode?: "add" (default) | "subtract" | "smooth", frame?} → {bone, changed, bound}. The Bind tool's brush: raises, lowers or evens out how much the bone moves the shape's points within the radius of each dab (a smooth falloff to the rim); each point's weights stay normalised (its other bones share what is left) and the points become hand-bound. A drag sends many in one gesture: one undo step

label: Pin Bone

label: Pose Bone

label: Remove Bone
params_doc: {bone} removes it and the bones below it → {removed, freed, unbound, layer, armature_removed}; the instances and shapes they moved go to a layer of their own as they look at the playhead (with the last bone, the whole armature does); a shape left with no bones inside stays as it looks there; asks first when the armature has more than one pose

label: Joint Limits
params_doc: {bone, constrain?: bool (false: turns freely), min?, max? (°, −360…360, from where it was drawn)} limits how far the joint turns, in every pose

label: Bone Spring
params_doc: {bone, strength? (0–100: 0 is no spring; stiffer swings faster and lags less), damping? (0–100: how quickly the swing dies down; 100 absorbs it all)} secondary motion: the bone lags behind and swings past its pose as the bones it hangs from move, then settles. Evaluated, never stored: the keyed poses don't change

label: Joint Translation
params_doc: {bone, axis: "x" | "y" (along the axes of what the bone starts on, as it is turned), enabled?: bool (false: the joint doesn't slide that way), constrain?: bool (false: slides freely), min?, max? (px, ±10,000, from where it was drawn)} lets the joint slide, in every pose; posing (bone.solve, the Selection tool) slides it only where turning can't reach

label: Set Point Weight

Hand-bound

label: Brush Stroke
params_doc: {points: [[x, y], [x, y, pressure 0..1 (clamped)] or [x, y, pressure, altitude, azimuth] (the pen's tilt in degrees: altitude 90 upright to 0 flat, azimuth the way it leans, clockwise from +x)], ..] (one point paints a dab), preset? (a brush from brush.preset_list, by key or name: its settings are the defaults for the rest), size? (stage units, default 10), shape?: round|square, angle? (degrees), roundness? (5..100 %, default 100), smoothing? (0..100, default 50), curve?: linear|soft|firm|[[pressure, output], ..] (how pressure maps, both 0..1), pressure_size? (default true: pressure varies the size from 10 to 100 %), pressure_opacity? (default false: the stroke's average pressure sets its opacity), taper_start?, taper_end? (0..50 % of the stroke's length), spacing? (0 continuous, or 5..1000 % of the size between dabs), jitter? (0..50 % of the size: a ragged edge), texture? (0..100 %: a paper grain of holes through the paint), scatter? (0..200 % of the size: dabs thrown either side of the line, varied in size), tilt_angle? (the pen's tilt turns the tip: its angle plus the azimuth), tilt_width? (the pen's tilt widens the tip, up to twice as wide flat; also the Paint Brush's width), as_stroke? (default false; true: the Paint Brush, a variable-width stroke in the stroke colour, editable with the Width tool), mode?: normal|fills|behind|selection|inside (Paint Normal covers fills and lines, Paint Fills leaves lines, Paint Behind paints only empty areas, Paint Selection only inside the selected fills, Paint Inside only inside the fill the stroke starts on or the empty area closed off around it; ADR 0080), color? (default: the fill colour, or the stroke colour as a stroke), unit? (stage units per screen point, default 1: smoothing and accuracy follow it), object? (default the Object Drawing setting; a fill that is not fully opaque is its own shape, so it composites over what is behind it)}

params_doc: {from, to} moves the filter at index `from` (0 is the first, applied first) to index `to` in the lists of the selected movie clips, buttons and text; the order changes how they draw

label: Paste Filters
params_doc: {replace? (default false: added after their own)} pastes the copied filters onto the selected movie clips, buttons and text

label: Apply Filter Preset
params_doc: {name: one of yours, or a built-in one (Soft Shadow, Hard Shadow, Neon Glow, Outline, Emboss, Engrave, Soft Focus, Greyscale)} gives the selected movie clips, buttons and text the preset's filters, replacing theirs (as Animate does)

label: Delete Filter Preset
params_doc: {name} deletes a filter preset of yours (asks first: it can't be undone; artwork that used it keeps its filters). Built-in presets can't be deleted, only hidden (filter.preset_hide)

label: Export Filter Presets
params_doc: {path, names? (default: all of yours; built-in ones may be named)} writes filter presets to a small JSON file

label: Hide Built-in Filter Preset
params_doc: {name, hidden? (default true; false shows it again)} hides a built-in filter preset from the presets menu, or shows it again (kept in your preferences; a hidden preset still applies by name)

label: Import Filter Presets
params_doc: {path} adds the presets in a filter preset file to yours (a name you have already gets a number)

label: Filter Presets
params_doc: {} → {presets: your filter presets, each a name and its filters; builtin: the built-in ones (ADR 0099), each with its name, filters and whether you have hidden it}

label: Rename Filter Preset
params_doc: {name, to} (your own presets; the built-in ones keep their names)

label: Save Filter Preset
params_doc: {name, filters? (a list as element.set_filters takes; default: the selected object's)} saves a filter preset of your own (kept in your preferences; a name you have already is replaced, after asking; a built-in preset's name is refused)

label: Remove Filter
params_doc: {index? (default: every filter)} removes a filter from the selected movie clips, buttons and text

label: Go to Found Item
params_doc: {layer?: id (its scene or symbol is found), scene?: index, symbol?: id, path?: [{layer, frame, element}] (instances to open in place from `scene`, or from `symbol` opened alone), frame?, element?} goes there: closes open symbols, switches scene or opens the symbol (in place through an instance that uses it when there is one), picks the layer and frame and selects the element

label: Replace
params_doc: {the find.search query, with: text (kind text; $1 and ${name} insert groups when regex) | family (font) | #rrggbb (color; each place keeps its alpha) | library id (symbol, sound, bitmap), at?: one hit as find.search returned it (Replace); without `at`, every hit (Replace All, one undo step; asks first above 100 places)} → {replaced, skipped, notes}

label: Find and Replace
params_doc: {kind: text | font | color | symbol | sound | bitmap, text? (kind text: what to find), match_case?, whole_word?, regex? (a pattern; linear-time engine, size-limited), font? (family), color? (#rrggbb; alpha is ignored), symbol? | sound? | bitmap?: library id, in?: [text, labels, layers, instances, scripts] (kind text) | [fills, strokes, text] (kind color) (default: all), scope?: scene (the current scene and the symbols it uses; default) | document, offset?, limit? (default 500, at most 10000)} → {hits: [{kind, field, scene | symbol, layer, layer_name, frame (keyframe start; null on a layer name), element?, start, end (characters, text only), found, context}], total, truncated}

label: Align on Multiple Frames
params_doc: {first, last, edge: left|hcenter|right|top|vcenter|bottom, items?, to_stage? (default: one item aligns to the stage), merge?} lines the items up with the edge of their bounds together (or the stage's), each on its own keyframe

label: Artwork on Multiple Frames
params_doc: {first, last} lists every element Edit Multiple Frames shows in frames first..=last (0-based): [layer, frame (its keyframe's first frame), id] with stage bounds; the playhead's elements as they look there

label: Copy on Multiple Frames
params_doc: {first, last, items?} copies the items (default: everything shown), remembering each one's keyframe: Paste on Multiple Frames puts them back keyframe by keyframe, Paste puts them all on the current frame

label: Cut on Multiple Frames
params_doc: {first, last, items?} frames.copy, then frames.delete

label: Clear on Multiple Frames
params_doc: {first, last, items?} deletes the items (default: everything shown) from their keyframes

label: Move on Multiple Frames
params_doc: {first, last, dx, dy, items?: [[layer, frame, id], ..], merge?: bool} moves artwork on every keyframe within frames first..=last (0-based) on visible, unlocked layers, as Edit Multiple Frames does: the items given (a keyframe's first frame and an element id), or all of them; a motion tween's path and X/Y keys move with its object; raw shapes merge again where they land unless merge is false; one undo step; answers the items after the move

label: Merge on Multiple Frames
params_doc: {first, last, items} the raw shapes among the items merge again with what they touch on their keyframes (the end of a drag made with merge: false); answers the items after the merge

label: Paste in Place on Multiple Frames
params_doc: {first, last, layer?} pastes in place onto the keyframes within the markers: artwork copied from several keyframes onto the keyframe covering the frame each came from (on the layers it came from when it came from several, else on `layer` or the active layer); artwork copied on one frame onto every keyframe of the layer; raw shapes merge where they land

label: Transform on Multiple Frames
params_doc: {first, last, items?, merge?, a, b, c, d, e, f} (an affine in stage space) | {rotate? (degrees), scale_x?, scale_y?, skew_x?, skew_y? (degrees), pivot?: [x, y] (default: the centre of every item's bounds together)} transforms the items on each keyframe about one shared pivot, as Free Transform does with Edit Multiple Frames on; one undo step

label: Instance Name
params_doc: {element?: id (default: the selected instance), name: letters, digits, _ or $, not starting with a digit; "" clears} names a movie clip or button instance, or a dynamic or input text field, for actions and scripts

label: Add Classic Motion Guide
params_doc: {layer?}

label: Delete Layer
params_doc: {layer? (a folder goes with its contents)}

label: Layer Depths
params_doc: {frame?} → {camera: bool, layers: [{layer, name, depth, keyed, key_here, attached}]} the layers that can have a depth, nearest first (ties in timeline order), at the frame

label: Move Layer To
params_doc: {layer?, before?: layer id | after?: layer id | into?: folder id} moves a layer anywhere in the stack, as a drag in the timeline does; a folder, mask or guide moves with everything in it. before / after: it lands just above that layer, or just below it and whatever it holds, beside it (in the same folder, or under the same mask or guide: normal layers only). into: it becomes the first layer in that folder. None of them: the bottom of the stack, outside every folder

label: Move Layer Down
params_doc: {layer?}

label: Move Layer Up
params_doc: {layer?}

label: New Layer
params_doc: {name?}

label: New Folder
params_doc: {name?}

label: Get Layer Properties
params_doc: {layer?} the layer's name, type, mask type (mask layers), colour, outline, height (percent), visible, locked and onion

label: Remove Depth Key
params_doc: {layer?, frame? (default: the playhead)} removes the layer's depth key at the frame; removing the last one leaves the depth it had there

label: Rename Layer
params_doc: {name, layer?}

label: Select Layer
params_doc: {layer: id} or {index}, select?: bool (also select all of its artwork at the playhead, as a click on the layer's name does; nothing on a locked or hidden layer)

label: Attach Layer to Camera
params_doc: {attached?: bool (default: toggles), layer?} an attached layer stays where it is on screen while the camera moves (titles, HUDs); its depth plays no part (ADR 0082)

label: Layer Colour
params_doc: {color: "#rrggbb", layer?} the layer's colour: its outlines in outline mode and its bar on the timeline

label: Layer Depth
params_doc: {depth (px behind the stage, −500…10000; through the camera a deeper layer moves and scales less, and draws behind nearer ones), layer?, key?: bool (default: whether the layer's depth is keyed), frame? (default: the playhead)} with `key` sets a depth key at the frame (the first key away from frame 0 also keys frame 0 with the depth it had), so the depth tweens linearly between keys; `key: false` makes the depth one value again (ADR 0082)

label: Layer Height
params_doc: {height: 100 | 200 | 300 (percent of a normal row), layer?} the layer's row height on the timeline

label: Mask Type
params_doc: {mask: coverage|alpha|luminance, layer?} how a mask layer reveals the layers it masks: coverage (its fills' area), alpha (its artwork's opacity: gradients and faded shapes make soft edges) or luminance (its brightness: white shows, black hides; SVG's mask) (ADR 0070)

label: Onion Skin Layer
params_doc: {onion?: bool (default: the other way), solo?: bool, layer?} whether onion skin draws the layer's frames around the playhead. solo: only this layer is onion-skinned (every other layer off); solo again on the only layer on turns them all back on (Alt-click)

label: Layer Properties
params_doc: {layer?, name?, type?: normal|mask|masked|guide|guided, mask?: coverage|alpha|luminance (a mask layer's mask type), color?, outline?: bool (view as outlines), height?: 100|200|300, visible?, locked?, onion?} sets several at once, as one undo step; answers with the layer's properties

label: Layer Type
params_doc: {type: normal|mask|masked|guide|guided, layer?}

label: Layer Volume
params_doc: {volume? (0–1: the layer's sounds and those in the symbols on it), muted?, layer?}

label: Lock/Unlock Layer
params_doc: {layer?, on?: bool (default: the other way), all?: true (every layer but the camera, as the padlock above the layers: unlocks them all when all are locked, else locks them all)}

label: Mask
params_doc: {layer?}

label: Mute/Unmute Layer
params_doc: {layer?} (its sounds, and those in the symbols on it, go silent in playback and every export)

label: Outline Layer
params_doc: {layer?, on?: bool (default: the other way), all?: true (every layer but the camera, as the square above the layers: back to artwork when all are outlines, else all as outlines)}

label: Show/Hide Layer
params_doc: {layer?, on?: bool (default: the other way), all?: true (every layer but the camera, as the eye above the layers: hides them all when all show, else shows them all)}

label: Delete
params_doc: {items: [{symbol | bitmap | sound | folder: id}, ..]} deletes items and folders with everything in them; instances of deleted symbols, shapes filled with deleted bitmaps and keyframes' deleted sounds go too (asks first when anything deleted is in use or a folder isn't empty)

label: Delete Unused Items
params_doc: {} deletes every item `library.unused` lists (asks first)

label: Duplicate Symbol
params_doc: {symbol, name? (default: “<name> copy”)} → {symbol, name}: a copy in the same folder, with its own layers and elements and no linkage class

label: List Library
params_doc: {} every folder (id, name, parent, path) and item (symbol | bitmap | sound id, kind, name, folder, path, uses, unused) in Library order; `uses` counts instances, bitmap fills and keyframe sounds once per keyframe

label: Move to Folder
params_doc: {items: [{symbol | bitmap | sound | folder: id}, ..], to: folder id | null (the top level)} moves items and folders (with what they hold) into a folder; a folder can't go inside itself, and a name the folder already has stops the move

label: New Folder
params_doc: {name? (default: the next free “Folder n”), parent?: folder id} → {folder, name}; names are unique within a folder (case aside) and can't hold “/”

label: Place on Stage
params_doc: {symbol | bitmap | sound: id, x?, y?} or {items: [{symbol | bitmap | sound: id}, ..], x?, y?} → {element, elements, sound?}: symbols and bitmaps centred on x, y (default: the stage centre; inside an open symbol, in its space) in the active layer's keyframe at the playhead, selected; a sound goes onto that keyframe, its span grown to fit (one sound per keyframe). One undo step

label: Rename
params_doc: {symbol | bitmap | sound | folder: id, name} renames a Library item or folder; the name must be free in its folder (case aside) and can't hold “/”

label: Allow Smoothing
params_doc: {bitmap, on?: bool (default: toggle)} whether the bitmap is filtered when scaled or turned (off: hard-edged pixels)

label: Select Unused Items
params_doc: {} → {items: [..]} the items nothing in the movie reaches: not in a scene, nor inside a symbol that is; symbols with a linkage class count as used

label: Delete Saved Command
params_doc: {folder, name, confirm}: deletes a saved command's file (cannot be undone)

label: List History Steps
params_doc: {} → {steps: [{index, label, undone, keep, commands?, why?, rewritten?}]}: every undo-history step as Save As Command keeps it: `keep` false says `why` it can't be kept; `rewritten` names params dropped so the step acts on the selection or active layer

label: Add Saved Command from File
params_doc: {folder, path (a saved command's file), name? (default: the file's), confirm? (to replace one of that name)} → {name, path, steps}: checks it and copies it in, last in the list

label: Manage Saved Commands…
params_doc: {folder} → {commands: [{name, path, steps}], problems: [{file, error}]}: the saved commands in the folder, in their order (the app shows them in a window)

label: Move Saved Command
params_doc: {folder, name, index (its new place in the list, 0-based)}

label: Rename Saved Command
params_doc: {folder, name, to} → {name, from, path}: renames a saved command (its file); its place in the list stays

label: Run Command…
params_doc: {name + folder (a saved command) | path (a saved command's file, or a JSON array of {cmd, params}) | steps: [{cmd, params?, label?}], name? (for steps)} → {name, steps, results}: runs the steps in order as one undo step named after it. At the first step that fails nothing is changed and the error names the step. Steps may call what a plug-in may, never macro.*

label: Save As Command…
params_doc: {folder, name, history: [index, ..] (as macro.history lists them) | steps: [{cmd, params?, label?}], confirm? (to replace a saved command of that name)} → {name, path, steps, rewritten}: keeps the steps as <folder>/<name>.json, last in the list

label: Break Apart
params_doc: {} the selected symbol instances become their contents, text becomes shapes, and drawing objects become raw shapes that merge with the raw shapes they touch

label: Combine Objects
params_doc: {op: union|intersect|punch|crop} combines the selected shapes on the active layer, bottom to top as they are stacked (ADR 0073). union: one drawing object of everything (a group of the merged pieces when they have more than one colour or keep lines); intersect: the area every one covers, in the topmost's fill and stroke; punch: the topmost's area cut out of each of the others; crop: each of the others cut to the topmost's area. Punch and crop remove the topmost. A result of one fill (or one line) is a drawing object, one of several is a group of raw shapes → {op, created}

label: Convert to Symbol…
params_doc: {name? (default: the next free “Symbol n”; a name the folder holds gets a number), kind?: graphic|movie_clip|button (default: graphic), folder?: Library folder id (default: the top level)} → {symbol, instance, name, layer, folder} (a selection on several layers becomes one symbol with those layers inside; the instance lands on the topmost)

label: Crop
params_doc: {} combine with op crop

label: Envelope
params_doc: {} opens an envelope around the selected shapes and drawing objects on the active layer (ADR 0080): a mesh of 4 × 4 Bézier control points over their bounds, at rest → {points: [[x, y] × 16] (row by row from the top-left), bounds: [x, y, w, h], shapes}. Then modify.envelope_move bends them. Symbols, text, groups and bitmaps can't be bent: break them apart first

label: Close Envelope
params_doc: {} closes the open envelope: bent raw shapes merge with the drawing they now touch (as after a move). Nothing to close is no error → {closed}

label: Envelope
params_doc: {points: [[x, y] × 16] (the whole mesh) | index: 0..15, x, y (one control point; a corner or side handle moves the inner points with it, as a Coons patch), tolerance? (stage units, default 0.05)} bends the open envelope's shapes from where they were when it opened → {points, shapes}. One undo step

label: Group
params_doc: {} puts the selected elements on each layer into one group there (ADR 0073), where the topmost of them was, and selects it → {group, members} (one layer) or {layers: [..]}. Members keep their places exactly. The group's registration point is the centre of what was grouped, and members are stored relative to it. Raw shapes inside merge only with each other; double-click the group (symbol.edit) to edit it in place

label: Intersect
params_doc: {} combine with op intersect

label: Punch
params_doc: {} combine with op punch

label: Transform
params_doc: {a, b, c, d, e, f} affine applied in stage space (free transform), to the selection on every layer

label: Ungroup
params_doc: {} puts each selected group's members back on its layer where it was, each placed and coloured as the group showed it, and selects them; raw shapes among them merge with the drawing there → {members}

label: Union
params_doc: {} combine with op union

label: Add Motion Path Point
params_doc: {x, y, slop? (stage units, default 4) | segment, t (0..1), layer?, frame?}: an anchor on the motion path, its shape unchanged → {anchor}

label: Remove Motion Path
params_doc: {layer?, frame?}: back to the straight path the X/Y curves trace

label: Convert Motion Path Point
params_doc: {anchor, smooth: bool, layer?, frame?}: smooth (handles in line) or corner (handles on the anchor)

label: Delete Motion Path Points
params_doc: {anchors: [index, ..] (as motion.info lists them; the ends stay), layer?, frame?}: the path refits through the rest

label: Motion Tween
params_doc: {layer?, frame?} → the span's properties, keys, eases and values at the frame, its motion path, its anchors pinned to frames (pins) and where the object is

label: Join Motion
params_doc: {layer?, frame?, to? (the last frame of the spans to join; default: the span after the one at the frame)}: adjacent motion tweens of one object become one, keeping every frame as it was → {start, frames, joined}

label: Move Property Keyframes
params_doc: {keys: [{property, frame}, ..] (frames as motion.info lists them), by (frames; negative = earlier), layer?, frame? (in the span; default: the first key's)}: values and eases travel with their keys; no key moves outside the span or onto or past a key of its property that isn't moving (the move stops there); a pinned path point's X and Y keys move together → {by, keys}

label: Move Motion Path
params_doc: {dx, dy, layer?, frame?}: the whole path with its object, keeping the timing

label: Orient to Path
params_doc: {orient: bool, layer?, frame?}: turn the object as its motion path turns

label: Pin Motion Path Point
params_doc: {anchor? (default: a new anchor where the object is), frame? (the frame to pin it to, between the first and last position keys), layer?}: the object passes the anchor exactly on that frame → {anchor, frame, pins}

label: Remove Property Keyframe
params_doc: {property? (default: every property; a filter colour such as filter.0.color names its four channels), frame?, layer?}

label: Property Ease
params_doc: {easing (as timeline.set_easing takes it, saved eases too), property? (default: every property; a filter colour such as filter.0.color names its four channels), frame? (inside the segment), layer?} (stepped properties hold their keys and take no ease)

label: Property Keyframe
params_doc: {property: x|y|scale_x|scale_y|rotation|skew|alpha|brightness|tint (amount)|tint_red|tint_green|tint_blue (0..255)|red_multiplier|green_multiplier|blue_multiplier|alpha_multiplier (%)|red_offset|green_offset|blue_offset|alpha_offset (-255..255)|filter.<slot>.<blur_x|blur_y|strength (%)|angle|distance|brightness|contrast|saturation|hue> (a number of the object's filter at that place, 0 the first; ADR 0092)|filter.<slot>.<color|shadow_color|highlight_color|stop_<n>>_<red|green|blue (0..255)|alpha (%)> (a channel of one of the filter's colours, stop_0 the ramp's first stop)|filter.<slot>.<quality (1..3)|inner|knockout|hide_object (0 or 1)> (stepped: a key holds until the next one; ADR 0099), value (px, %, °), frame?, layer?} or {property: filter.<slot>.<color|shadow_color|highlight_color|stop_<n>>, color: "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa"} to key a filter colour's four channels at once (colour properties of several styles compose into Advanced, ADR 0056)

label: Edit Motion Path
params_doc: {d: SVG path data in stage space (its first subpath; ends are the start and end positions), layer?, frame?}

label: Split Motion
params_doc: {layer?, frame?}: the motion tween becomes two at the frame, each moving as before → {first, second}

label: Unpin Motion Path Point
params_doc: {anchor? | frame?, layer?}: the anchor shapes the path only again; the X/Y keys of its frame go → {anchor, frame, pins}

label: Apply Style
params_doc: {fill?: bool, stroke?: bool} (default both) gives the selected shapes the fill swatch's paint (shapes with a fill) and the stroke settings (shapes with a line, and drawing objects without one)

label: Paint Bucket
params_doc: {x, y, color?, gap? (stage units: how wide an opening still counts as closed), object?: bool} fills the closed area under the point, or recolours the fill there; unless `object` (default: the Object Drawing setting), the fill is raw and merges with the drawing (an area closed by raw lines and fills is filled exactly up to them)

label: Ink Bottle
params_doc: {x, y, color?, width?, profile?, cap?, join?, miter?, style?, dash?, dash_offset?, dot_spacing?} (the tool's line style unless given; see stroke.set_style)

label: Lock Fill
params_doc: {on?: bool (default: toggle)} Lock Fill: a gradient or bitmap from the fill swatch is poured where it lies on the stage, running on across shapes; off, each shape gets it fitted to its bounds → {on}

label: Eyedropper
params_doc: {x, y, other?: bool (into the other swatch only: a fill's colour into the stroke, a line's into the fill), slop?} picks the style under the point on any visible layer into the tool settings: a fill's paint (solid, gradient or bitmap, kept where it is on the stage) into the fill swatch, a line's colour, width and profile into the stroke settings

label: Fill
params_doc: {type?: solid|linear|radial|bitmap (default: the swatch's), color? (solid, "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa"), stops?: [{offset: 0..1, color: "#rrggbb" | "#rrggbbaa"}, ..] (2 to 15; each stop has its own alpha), spread?: extend|reflect|repeat, linear_rgb?: bool, focal?: -0.98..0.98 (radial), bitmap?: id, selection?: bool (default true)} sets the fill swatch (what new shapes, the Paint Bucket and the Brush pour) and, unless `selection` is false, the fills of the selected shapes. A shape keeping its kind of fill keeps where its gradient or bitmap lies; one changing kind gets it fitted to its bounds. A new gradient starts white to black → {fill: {type, ..}, changed}

label: Gradient Transform
params_doc: {element?: id (default: the selected shapes with a gradient or bitmap fill), frame?: [a, b, c, d, e, f] (the fill's frame in the space being edited: the box -1..1 onto a linear gradient's span, a radial gradient's ring or one copy of a bitmap), or changes made in this order: scale_x?, scale_y?, scale? (along the frame's own axes), skew_x?, skew_y? (degrees, along its axes), rotate? (degrees, about its centre), move?: [dx, dy], center?: [x, y]; focal?: -0.98..0.98 (radial)} moves, turns, scales or skews where a gradient or bitmap fill lies, as the Gradient Transform tool (F) does → {changed, frames: [[a, b, c, d, e, f], ..]}

label: Add Anchor Point
params_doc: {id, x, y, slop?}

label: Bend Segment
params_doc: {x, y, dx, dy, id?, cmd?, t?, slop?, merge?: bool} the segment at (x, y) (of shape `id`, else the one there) bends so that point moves by (dx, dy), its ends staying; a raw shape's copies of the edge bend with it and merge again (unless merge is false)

label: Convert Anchor Point
params_doc: {id, cmd, smooth: bool}

label: Delete Anchor Points
params_doc: {id, cmds: [..]}

label: Move Points
params_doc: {id, points: [[cmd, slot], ..], dx, dy, smooth?: bool} (a handle moved alone at a smooth anchor turns the other one with it, keeping its length, unless smooth is false: Alt breaks the pair)

label: Install Plug-in…
params_doc: {path: a .wasm plug-in, confirm? (when it replaces an installed plug-in's file)} validates and installs it; with a plug-ins folder it is copied there

label: Manage Plug-ins…
params_doc: {} lists the installed plug-ins (the app shows them in a window)

label: Reload Plug-ins
params_doc: {folder? (makes it the plug-ins folder first)} re-reads every .wasm in the plug-ins folder

label: Remove Plug-in
params_doc: {id, confirm? (when it deletes the plug-in's file from the plug-ins folder)}

label: Run Plug-in
params_doc: {id, params?: {…} (see plugin.list; missing ones take their defaults)} one undo step

label: Clear Recent Files
params_doc: {pinned? (default false: pinned favourites stay)} → {removed}

label: Pin to Recent Files
params_doc: {index? | path?, pinned? (default: toggle)}: a pinned file stays at the top of Open Recent

label: Remove from Recent Files
params_doc: {index? | path?}

label: Publish Settings…
params_doc: {} (the document's publish profile, and where each format would go)

label: Publish Settings
params_doc: {profile? (a whole profile, as publish.settings_get returns it), format? (html | gif | apng | webp | video | lottie | sprite_sheet | png_sequence | png | svg | audio), enabled?, output? (relative to the document's folder; {name} is the document's name), and that format's options: title, sound, fit (html); from, to, scale, loop (gif); from, to, scale, loop (true, false or how many times it plays; 0: forever), background (apng, webp); from, to, scale, audio (video); from, to, background (lottie); from, to, scale, columns, padding, background (sprite_sheet); from, to, scale (png_sequence); frame, scale (png); frame (svg); from, to, rate, bits (audio). from/to/frame are movie frames, null for the movie's ends}

label: Add Anchor Point
params_doc: {x, y, slop?} adds an anchor on the raw line or fill edge at (x, y): every raw shape with that edge gets it, and the curve keeps its shape; returns where it is

label: Convert Anchor Points
params_doc: {points: [[x, y], ..], smooth: bool} makes the raw anchors at those positions smooth (their handles in one line) or corners (handles drawn in), in every shape that has them

label: Delete Anchor Points
params_doc: {points: [[x, y], ..]} deletes the raw anchors at those positions (as raw.points lists them): every shape that has one is joined across it, so the drawing stays connected; a free end shortens its line; a shape left with nothing is removed; a point where three or more edges meet is kept

label: Selection Tool Target
params_doc: {x, y, slop?, point_slop?} what a Selection-tool drag from (x, y) takes: a point, a segment to bend, a fill, or an object

label: Merge Shapes
params_doc: {ids?: [..]} the raw shapes (default: the selection) merge again with the raw shapes they touch, in place

label: Move Handle
params_doc: {id, cmd, slot: 1|2, dx, dy, smooth?: bool, merge?: bool} moves a handle (control point `slot` of segment `cmd` of shape `id`, as `raw.points` lists it) by (dx, dy): the curve changes in every raw shape that has that edge, and they merge again (unless merge is false); at a smooth anchor the other handle turns to stay opposite, keeping its length (unless smooth is false: Alt breaks the pair)

label: Move Point
params_doc: {x, y, to_x, to_y, with?: [[x, y], ..], points?: [[id, cmd], ..], snap?, slop?, merge?: bool} moves the corner or end at (x, y), with every raw shape that shares it, to (to_x, to_y), snapped within `snap` to points, lines and fill edges (while Snap to Objects is on); the anchors at `with` move by as much; returns the points to pass on while a drag goes on

label: Raw Points
params_doc: {ids?: [..]} the anchors of raw shapes (default: the selection), once per position, and the handles of their curved segments

label: Select Parts
params_doc: {x0, y0, x1, y1, add?: bool} the marquee, on every visible, unlocked layer: the parts of raw fills and strokes under the rectangle (cut at its edges, per layer) and the objects wholly inside it

label: Subselect
params_doc: {x, y, add?: bool, slop?} the Subselection tool's click: the raw stroke or fill at (x, y) and every raw shape connected to it are selected, to show their anchors (an object there is selected alone); returns the anchors and, on an edge, its ends

label: Subselect Rectangle
params_doc: {x0, y0, x1, y1, add?: bool} the Subselection tool's marquee, on the active layer only: the shapes it touches are selected whole (raw ones with every raw shape connected to them); returns the raw anchors inside it

label: Delete Scene
params_doc: {scene?}

label: Duplicate Scene
params_doc: {scene?}

label: Move Scene Later
params_doc: {scene?}

params_doc: {scene?}

params_doc: {name?}

params_doc: {name, scene?}

params_doc: {scene: index}

label: Check Frame Script
params_doc: {text: the script, language?: actionscript3|actionscript1or2|other (default actionscript3)} whether it would run (the ActionScript 3.0 subset, ADR 0013), its problems with line and column, what is ignored, the names it takes from other frames of its timeline (`uses`), and what it compiles to (`steps`, `program`); changes nothing

label: Clear Frame Script
params_doc: {symbol?, layer?, frame?} removes the keyframe's kept script (actions are left alone: actions.clear)

label: List Frame Scripts
params_doc: {text?: bool (default true)} every kept script in every scene and symbol, with its text, whether it runs and its problems, plus symbol linkage classes and the document class

label: Set Frame Script
params_doc: {text?: the script, verbatim ("" clears; at most 1 MiB), language?: actionscript3|actionscript1or2|other (default: the script's, else actionscript3), symbol?: id, layer?, frame?} keeps a script on the keyframe at the frame (it replaces actions there); ActionScript 3.0 in the subset runs in Test Movie and the HTML export, the rest is kept and not run (`runs`, `problems` say which)

label: Set Script Class
params_doc: {symbol?: id (default: the document), class: dotted class name ("" clears), base?: the class it extends} sets a symbol's linkage class, or the document class; kept as text, not run

label: Delete Sound
params_doc: {sound} (from the library and every keyframe that uses it)

label: Place Sound
params_doc: {sound, layer?, frame? (a blank keyframe is made there if the frame is empty), sync?: event|start|stop|stream, repeat?, loop?, effect?, envelope?, extend? (lengthen the layer's last span to the sound's length)}

label: Remove Sound
params_doc: {layer?, frame?}

label: Rename Sound
params_doc: {sound, name}

label: Sound Settings
params_doc: {layer?, frame?, sound?: id | null (null takes the sound off), sync?, repeat?, loop?, effect?: none|left_channel|right_channel|fade_left_to_right|fade_right_to_left|fade_in|fade_out|custom (presets shape over the time the sound is heard; custom starts from the effect before), envelope?: [{at (seconds from the sound's start), left (0–1), right (0–1)}…] (1–16 points; makes the effect custom)}

label: Delete Width Point
params_doc: {id, index}

label: Width Profile
params_doc: {profile: uniform|taper_both|taper_start|taper_end|bulge|pinch | [[t, left, right], ..], id? (default: the selected shapes)}

label: Stroke Style
params_doc: {cap?: none|round|square, join?: miter|round|bevel, miter? (limit, 1..=100; a corner whose point is longer than this many widths is bevelled), style?: solid|dashed|dotted, dash? ([on, off, ..] lengths in the shape's units; implies dashed), dash_offset?, dot_spacing? (between dots, edge to edge; implies dotted), id? (default: the selected shapes)}

label: Width
params_doc: {id, index? (an existing point; else one is added), t? 0..1 | x, y (stage point on the stroke), left?, right?, width? (both sides; factors of the nominal width)}

label: Width at Point
params_doc: {x, y, id? (default: the topmost stroke there on the active layer), slop?}

label: Add Swatch
params_doc: {from?: fill|stroke (default fill: the fill swatch's colour or gradient; stroke: the stroke colour), or the swatch itself: type?: solid|linear|radial, color? ("#rrggbb" | "#rrggbbaa", solid), stops?: [{offset: 0..1, color}, ..] (2 to 15), spread?: extend|reflect|repeat, linear_rgb?: bool, focal?: -0.98..0.98 (radial); name?, at? (index; default: the end)} → {index, count}

label: Apply Swatch
params_doc: {index, target?: fill|stroke (default fill), selection?: bool (default true)} sets the fill swatch (as paint.set_fill: a gradient is fitted to each shape) or the stroke colour, and unless `selection` is false the selected shapes' fills or strokes. A gradient swatch can't be a stroke (strokes are one colour) → {target, changed}

label: Clear Swatches
params_doc: {} removes every swatch but black and white (Animate's Clear Colors; undoable)

label: Duplicate Swatch
params_doc: {index} puts a copy right after it → {index, count}

label: Export Swatches
params_doc: {path} writes the document's swatches to a swatch file (JSON) → {written, swatches}

label: Import Swatches
params_doc: {path: a swatch file (.json, from swatch.export) or a GIMP palette (.gpl), replace?: bool (default false: added at the end)} → {imported, count}

label: Swatches
params_doc: {} the document's swatches, in the Swatches panel's order → {swatches: [{index, name, type, color | stops, ..}], count}

label: Move Swatch
params_doc: {from, to} (indices: the swatch at `from` ends up at `to`) → {index}

label: Delete Swatch
params_doc: {index} → {count}

label: Rename Swatch
params_doc: {index, name} (empty: no name, the hex shows on hover)

label: Default Swatches
params_doc: {} replaces the swatches with a new document's set (undoable)

label: Edit Symbols
params_doc: {id?: instance element id, symbol?: library symbol id} opens a symbol's timeline for editing: the instance `id` (default: the selected instance) in place, or a Library symbol at the stage's centre. A group (ADR 0073) or a drawing object (ADR 0080) opens in place the same way: inside, its raw shapes merge only with each other, and a drawing object closes as one object again (a group of its pieces when an edit left several). Every command then works inside it. With nothing to open while a symbol is open, goes back to the document (Animate's Ctrl+E)

label: Edit Document
params_doc: {all?: bool} closes the open symbol (default: one level; all: back to the scene), selecting the instance it was opened from

label: Symbol Type
params_doc: {kind: graphic|movie_clip|button, symbol?: id (default: the symbols of every selected instance)}

label: 9-Slice Scaling
params_doc: {symbol?: id (default: the symbol open for editing, else the selected instance's), on?: bool, left?, right?, top?, bottom? (guide positions in the symbol's space)} turns a symbol's guides for 9-slice scaling on or off, or moves them (ADR 0055). Turning them on brings back the guides it had when they were turned off (ADR 0057), else puts them a quarter of the way in from each edge of the symbol's artwork; moving one turns them on. Scaled instances then keep the corners outside the guides unscaled, stretch the edges one way and the centre both ways → {symbol, scale_grid: {left, right, top, bottom} | null}

label: Attach Text to Path
params_doc: {path?: element id of a shape (default: the other selected element, a shape), x?, y? (pick the shape at this stage point instead), offset? (px along the path; default by the text's alignment: its start, middle or end), flip?: bool} sets the selected static text along a copy of the shape's outline (its first contour); the shape stays as it is (ADR 0070)

label: Text Type
params_doc: {type?: static|dynamic|input, lines?: single|multiline|multiline_no_wrap|password (input only), width?, height? (the field's box, px), selectable?, border?, background?, border_color?, background_color?, max_chars? (input; 0: no limit), variable? (kept, not run)} on the selected text; dynamic and input fields are named with instance.set_name and scripted in Test Movie and the HTML export (ADR 0066)

label: Text on Path
params_doc: {offset? (px along the path), flip?: bool (along the path backwards, on its other side), release?: bool (back to lines of text where it starts)} on the selected text on a path (ADR 0070)

label: Release Text from Path
params_doc: {} the selected text on a path goes back to lines of text (ADR 0070)

label: Text Styles
params_doc: {start?, end? (characters; default: all)} of the first selected text: its runs, paragraphs, and what those characters share (a mixed value is null) (ADR 0085)

params_doc: {layer? | layers?: [..], frame?, count?}

label: Copy Frames
params_doc: {layer? | layers?: [..], frame?, count?}

label: Create Motion Tween
params_doc: {layer?, frame?} (several objects on the key become one graphic symbol; a one-frame span grows to a second)

label: Create Shape Tween
params_doc: {layer?, frame?, easing? (as timeline.set_easing takes it)}

label: Create Classic Tween
params_doc: {layer?, frame?, easing? (as timeline.set_easing takes it)}

params_doc: {layer? | layers?: [..], frame?, count?}

label: Frame
params_doc: {layer? | layers?: [..] | all_layers?: true (every layer with frames at or after the frame, as F5 with no frame selection; the active layer when none has), frame?, count?, advance?: true (the playhead moves onto the last frame inserted, as the key does in the editor)}

label: Keyframe
params_doc: {layer? | layers?: [..], frame?, advance?: true (on a keyframe the new key goes on the next frame, and the playhead moves onto it, as the key does in the editor)}

params_doc: {layer? | layers?: [..], from, to?, by, layer_by? (rows down; negative = up)}

(rows down; negative = up), copy?: true (Alt-drag: the frames stay where they were too)}: the spans starting in from..=to move whole, keeping their lengths and tweens (as dragging a tween span in Animate), replacing what they land on; the frames they leave are empty

label: Paste Frames
params_doc: {layer?, frame?} (top layer and first frame; default: active layer, playhead)

label: Remove Frame
params_doc: {layer? | layers?: [..], frame?, count?}

label: Remove Tween
params_doc: {layer?, frame?} (a motion tween leaves its object as it is on the first frame)

label: Set Tween Easing
params_doc: {easing: a preset name (Linear, QuadIn … ElasticInOut) | {classic: -100..100} | {bezier: [x1, y1, x2, y2]} | {custom: {points: [..]} | [[x, y], ..]} | {saved: name} | {plugin: id, ease: id} (an ease plug-in's; the tween keeps its sampled curve), group?: all|position|rotation|scale|color|filters (classic tweens: that property group's own ease), layer?, frame?}

params_doc: {label, layer?, frame?}

label: Orient to Path
params_doc: {orient: bool, layer?, frame?}

label: Add Shape Hint
params_doc: {layer?, frame? (in the shape tween, or the keyframe it ends on)} → the new hint's letter; it starts at the shapes' centre, unplaced

label: Remove All Hints
params_doc: {layer?, frame?}

label: Shape Hints
params_doc: {layer?, frame?} → the shape tween's hints: letter, start and end points, and whether each is on an edge

label: Move Shape Hint
params_doc: {hint: a..z, x, y, side?: start|end (default: the side the frame shows), layer?, frame?} (snaps to the nearest shape edge on that keyframe)

label: Remove Shape Hint
params_doc: {hint: a..z, layer?, frame?} (later letters move down one)

params_doc: {} whether the rulers, grid and guides show and snap, the grid's and guides' settings, and this scene's guides [{axis, at}, ..]

label: Edit Grid…
params_doc: {spacing?, spacing_x?, spacing_y? (stage pixels, 1..=4096), color?: "#rrggbb[aa]", over_objects?: bool, show?: bool, snap?: bool, accuracy?: "close"|"normal"|"distant"|"always"} sets the grid; spacing and colour are saved with the document (one undo step), the rest is the editor's; returns everything as view.aids does

label: Show Grid
params_doc: {on?: bool} (default: toggle) the grid on the stage (never in pictures or exports)

label: Snap to Grid
params_doc: {on?: bool} (default: toggle) points being drawn, dragged or moved snap to the grid's lines (shown or not)

params_doc: {axis: "horizontal"|"vertical", at} adds a guide to this scene at `at` stage pixels (y for a horizontal guide, x for a vertical one); returns {index, guides}

label: Delete Guide
params_doc: {index} removes this scene's guide `index`; refused while guides are locked

label: Move Guide
params_doc: {index, at} moves this scene's guide `index` (as view.aids lists them) to `at`; refused while guides are locked

label: Clear Guides
params_doc: {} removes every guide from this scene (undoable)

label: Lock Guides
params_doc: {on?: bool} (default: toggle) locked guides can't be dragged, moved or deleted one by one (new ones can still be added, and Clear Guides clears them)

label: Edit Guides…
params_doc: {color?: "#rrggbb[aa]", show?: bool, lock?: bool, snap?: bool, accuracy?: "close"|"normal"|"distant"} sets the guides; the colour is saved with the document (one undo step), the rest is the editor's; returns everything as view.aids does

label: Show Guides
params_doc: {on?: bool} (default: toggle) this scene's guides on the stage (never in pictures or exports)

label: Snap to Guides
params_doc: {on?: bool} (default: toggle) points being drawn, dragged or moved snap to the guides

label: Rulers
params_doc: {on?: bool} (default: toggle) rulers along the stage's top and left edges, in stage pixels from its top-left corner; drag from one to make a guide

label: Snap to Pixels
params_doc: {on?: bool} (default: toggle) points being drawn, dragged or moved go to whole stage pixels where nothing else snaps them

label: Add Warp Mesh
params_doc: {element? (a shape or bitmap; default the one selected), resolution? (cells along the longer side, 2…48; default 12)} → {element, created, resolution, columns, rows}. Covers the artwork with a warp mesh on every keyframe of its layer that holds it (it becomes a drawing object); on artwork that has one, changes the mesh's resolution

label: Warp Mesh
params_doc: {element?, frame?} → the artwork's warp at the frame: resolution, the mesh's columns, rows, vertices and triangles, whether it is bent, and its pins (id, where they show in stage px, and where they were placed on the artwork as drawn, in its own space)

label: Add Warp Pin
params_doc: {element?, x, y (stage px, on the artwork)} → {element, pin, created}. Pins the artwork there (adding the mesh first if it has none), on every keyframe that bends the same mesh; nothing moves

label: Move Warp Pin
params_doc: {element?, pin, x?, y? (stage px: where the pin goes), dx?, dy? (stage px: by how much), frame?} → {element, pin, at}. Bends the artwork at the frame (keying it inside a tween); pins tween between keyframes

label: Remove Warp Pin
params_doc: {element?, pin} removes the pin from every keyframe that bends the same mesh; the artwork follows the pins that are left

label: Remove Warp
params_doc: {element?} takes the warp mesh and its pins off the artwork on every keyframe of its layer: it shows as drawn again
